LAB SAFETY BASICSSafety is everyone's responsibility.
Before the Experiment
✔ Read all instructions carefully.
✔ Listen to your teacher.
✔ Tie back long hair.
✔ Wear safety goggles and a lab coat if required.
During the Experiment
✔ Follow instructions carefully.
✔ Handle equipment gently.
✔ Use chemicals only as directed.
✔ Keep your work area neat.
✔ Never taste or smell chemicals unless instructed.
✔ Do not run or play in the laboratory.
✔ Report spills or accidents immediately.
After the Experiment
✔ Turn off equipment if instructed.
✔ Clean your workspace.
✔ Wash your hands.
✔ Return equipment to its proper place.
MEASUREMENT SKILLS
Examples:
Measuring the length of a pencil in centimetres (cm) using a ruler.
Measuring the volume of water in millilitres (mL) using a measuring cylinder.
Measuring the mass of an object in grams (g) using a balance.
Measuring temperature in degrees Celsius (°C) using a thermometer.
Measuring time in seconds (s) using a stopwatch.

LAB SAFETY BASICSSafety is everyone's responsibility.
Before the Experiment
✔ Read all instructions carefully.
✔ Listen to your teacher.
✔ Tie back long hair.
✔ Wear safety goggles and a lab coat if required.
During the Experiment
✔ Follow instructions carefully.
✔ Handle equipment gently.
✔ Use chemicals only as directed.
✔ Keep your work area neat.
✔ Never taste or smell chemicals unless instructed.
✔ Do not run or play in the laboratory.
✔ Report spills or accidents immediately.
After the Experiment
✔ Turn off equipment if instructed.
✔ Clean your workspace.
✔ Wash your hands.
✔ Return equipment to its proper place.
MEASUREMENT SKILLS
Examples:
Measuring the length of a pencil in centimetres (cm) using a ruler.
Measuring the volume of water in millilitres (mL) using a measuring cylinder.
Measuring the mass of an object in grams (g) using a balance.
Measuring temperature in degrees Celsius (°C) using a thermometer.
Measuring time in seconds (s) using a stopwatch.

Design an Investigation
Investigation Topic
Research Question: How does the amount of light affect seed germination?
Your task is to design a safe and fair scientific investigation.
HINTS :

Keep the investigation fair
Everything should stay the same except the amount of light.
Think about:
Same type of seed
Same number of seeds
Same container
Same soil or cotton
Same amount of water
Same temperature
Same number of days

Materials
List everything you will need.Write quantities wherever possible.

Write your method as numbered steps.
Your procedure should explain:
How you will prepare the seeds
Where you will place each group
How often you will water them
How long you will observe them
What you will measure or record
How you will compare your results

Data Collection
Think about how you will record your observations.
You may record:
Number of seeds that germinated
Height of seedlings (cm)
Number of days taken to germinate
Daily observations
You can create your own observation table.

Safety
Remember to include safety precautions

assignments.title: LAB SAFETY BASICS
assignments.description:
We already discussed these in criterion B

LAB SAFETY BASICSSafety is everyone's responsibility.
Before the Experiment
✔ Read all instructions carefully.
✔ Listen to your teacher.
✔ Tie back long hair.
✔ Wear safety goggles and a lab coat if required.
During the Experiment
✔ Follow instructions carefully.
✔ Handle equipment gently.
✔ Use chemicals only as directed.
✔ Keep your work area neat.
✔ Never taste or smell chemicals unless instructed.
✔ Do not run or play in the laboratory.
✔ Report spills or accidents immediately.
After the Experiment
✔ Turn off equipment if instructed.
✔ Clean your workspace.
✔ Wash your hands.
✔ Return equipment to its proper place.
MEASUREMENT SKILLS
Examples:
Measuring the length of a pencil in centimetres (cm) using a ruler.
Measuring the volume of water in millilitres (mL) using a measuring cylinder.
Measuring the mass of an object in grams (g) using a balance.
Measuring temperature in degrees Celsius (°C) using a thermometer.
Measuring time in seconds (s) using a stopwatch.

assignments.title: Home Task – Criterion B (Strand iv)
assignments.description:
You can also pick any scenario of your CHOICE from cri B practice task sheet

Design an Investigation
Investigation Topic
Research Question: How does the amount of light affect seed germination?
Your task is to design a safe and fair scientific investigation.
HINTS :

Keep the investigation fair
Everything should stay the same except the amount of light.
Think about:
Same type of seed
Same number of seeds
Same container
Same soil or cotton
Same amount of water
Same temperature
Same number of days

Materials
List everything you will need.Write quantities wherever possible.

Write your method as numbered steps.
Your procedure should explain:
How you will prepare the seeds
Where you will place each group
How often you will water them
How long you will observe them
What you will measure or record
How you will compare your results

Data Collection
Think about how you will record your observations.
You may record:
Number of seeds that germinated
Height of seedlings (cm)
Number of days taken to germinate
Daily observations
You can create your own observation table.

Safety
Remember to include safety precautions
